rows.rationale: The bordered course slab reaches the full 1x1 footprint at ground height in all four rotations.
The opaque pond surround covers the full 1x1 footprint; retaining replace prevents grass bleed through the water asset.
The correctly sized garage and hardstanding fill one axis but leave a persistent exposed strip on the 0.880-cell axis; uniform scale would overflow.
The centred fenced yard fills one axis but leaves an exposed 0.886-cell short-axis band; a grass continuation is safer than scaling the architecture.
The complete hardstanding and curb slab reaches the footprint boundary across all rotations.
The authored vegetated base is effectively full-cell and visually continuous to every edge.
The centred terrace fills one axis but covers only 0.625 cells on the other; scaling would overflow the full axis substantially.
The concrete industrial slab reads as full-footprint; its sub-percent bevel inset does not expose a visible untreated strip.
The correctly sized tower compound leaves a thin but continuous exposed short-axis strip; scaling would overflow its full axis.
The block and base fill one axis but leave broad exposed bands on the 0.762-cell axis; uniform scale is unsafe.
The terrace base is effectively 1x1 and reaches the footprint outline in every rotation.
The grounded concrete podium fills one axis but leaves a consistent exposed strip on the 0.829-cell axis.
The intentionally asymmetric building, garden, and paths are correctly sized but do not provide a complete base; offset or scale would damage the composition.
The paved restaurant base is grounded but leaves a repeatable 0.911-cell edge band while the other axis is already full.
The house and landscaped plot are correctly sized but expose a short-axis strip; the existing garden makes a grass continuation natural.
The shop and paved forecourt fill one axis but leave a visible 0.902-cell outer band; scaling would overflow.
The 2x2 tower and podium are centred but cover only 1.757 cells in depth while already spanning the full two-cell width.
The walled landscaped base fills one axis but leaves a visible 0.846-cell short-axis strip across rotations.
The correctly sized theatre fills one axis but leaves broad exposed bands on the 0.645-cell axis; uniform scale would overflow.
The mandatory 2x2 checkpoint spans the full width but only 1.100 cells in depth; a footprint underlay repairs all four cells without unsafe scaling.
The walled grass plot fills one axis but exposes a persistent strip on its 0.907-cell near-ground axis; scaling would overflow.
The purpose-built grass plane fills the 1x1 footprint exactly.
The integrated terrain plate is effectively full-cell and exposes no meaningful footprint strip.
The vegetation is correctly scaled but its ground plate covers only about 0.844x0.791 cells; elevated trees already reach the full overall axis.
The full paved hardstanding covers the complete footprint and must continue replacing grass.
The paved fountain surround covers the complete footprint and must continue replacing grass.
The road and kerb plate covers the full 1x1 footprint.
The intersection hard surface covers the full 1x1 footprint.
The split-road hard surface covers the full 1x1 footprint.
The straight-road hard surface covers the full 1x1 footprint.
The straight-road hard surface remains full-footprint beneath its light posts.
